claimsVerified.claim: white-space sorts after text-wrap-mode and resets it; text-wrap-style is the load-bearing property
claimsVerified.evidence: src/sitespec/style-catalog.ts:101 re-emits token properties with Object.keys(source).sort(), and src/reconstruction/style-generator.ts declarations() sorts again before emitting. Empirical dump of a real generateStylesheet() call: `.wr-st000001{-webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;color:rgb(0,0,0);text-wrap-mode:wrap;text-wrap-style:balance;white-space:normal}` — white-space is LAST. Since `white-space` is the shorthand for white-space-collapse + text-wrap-mode, the emitted text-wrap-mode is indeed overwritten; `text-wrap-style` is NOT part of that shorthand, so `balance` survives. The suite's browser-stage line-box assertions therefore do prove wrapping is carried by text-wrap-style. Risk assessed BENIGN — see defect VV-05.

defects.description: Near-tautological guard: `check("no font binary / @font-face property was added", !STYLE_WHITELIST.some(p => p.startsWith("font-face") || p === "src"))` (scripts/smoke-visual-vocab.ts:471-474). No CSS property name can ever begin with "font-face", so that clause can never fail, and the check does not look for `font-display`, `@font-face`, or url()/binary values. The underlying CLAIM is true — I verified it directly from the diff — but this check does not meaningfully guard it.
defects.evidence: scripts/smoke-visual-vocab.ts:471-474; the 21-line diff of src/observer/types.ts contains no font-face, src, font-display or url() token.
defects.suggestedFix: assert against `font-display`, `src`, and any value containing `url(` in the emitted CSS, or drop the check and rely on the diff review.

defects.description: Label/assertion mismatch: `check("pseudo rules were emitted for all five fixture pseudos", pseudoStyles.ruleCount >= 5)` claims exactness but asserts a lower bound, so a spurious sixth rule would pass silently.
defects.suggestedFix: `=== 5`, or keep `>=` and retitle the check.

defects.description: One link of the chain is NOT production code: the clone's DOM comes from the suite's own `renderCompiledTree()` serializer rather than from src/reconstruction/compile-node.ts / generate-app.ts. This is disclosed honestly in the file header, and it is a reasonable substitution (the real emitter produces a React app requiring a build). The substitution stays faithful where it matters — class names come from the REAL styleClassName()/documentRootClassName() and the pseudo selectors are asserted against the REAL pseudoSelector() — and the five new properties travel through style TOKENS, not through DOM emission, so this stage cannot mask the change under test. It does mean the suite would not catch a divergence in real DOM emission.
defects.evidence: scripts/smoke-visual-vocab.ts renderCompiledTree(); header comment documents the substitution explicitly.

defects.description: Five checks are labeled `[darwin measurement]` but the suite has NO platform guard (no process.platform reference). If Chromium on a Linux CI runner computes `-webkit-font-smoothing` to anything other than `antialiased`, the suite hard-fails rather than skipping. Blink registers the property unconditionally, so it most likely computes identically on Linux — but that is unverified: this verification ran on Darwin only.
defects.evidence: grep for process.platform in scripts/smoke-visual-vocab.ts returns nothing; the five labeled checks are at lines 551, 598, 624, 767, 772.
defects.suggestedFix: gate the smoothing checks on process.platform === "darwin", or verify once on Linux and drop the label.

defects.description: `text-wrap-mode` is INERT in the generated CSS: alphabetical declaration ordering always emits the `white-space` shorthand after it, resetting it. The builder named this hazard and the assessment is correct — the two can only disagree for white-space-collapse/text-wrap-mode combinations that have no single white-space keyword (e.g. preserve-breaks + nowrap), and in that case Chromium's computed white-space serialization degrades rather than lying. `text-wrap-style` is unaffected by the white-space shorthand and is the property actually carrying balance. Recorded so a future change to declaration ordering or to either property is not assumed safe.
defects.evidence: empirical generateStylesheet() output: `.wr-st000001{-webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;color:rgb(0,0,0);text-wrap-mode:wrap;text-wrap-style:balance;white-space:normal}`; sorting at src/sitespec/style-catalog.ts:101 and src/reconstruction/style-generator.ts declarations().
